title: ThePrimeagen on why he ripped out Copilot and why AI is overrated for learning to code
summary: ThePrimeagen explains why he turned off Copilot after realizing he didn't actually know Go, why time in the saddle beats shortcuts, and why English-driven AI can't replace the precision of programming. He also covers how to treat AI job fears and why learning to code is a marathon.

principles.text: Copilot is fancy autocomplete; it can make you think you know a language you don't.
principles.quote: when I turned off co-pilot I realized I didn't know go I didn't I I Bamboozled myself into thinking I knew go I didn't know go and what I knew is how to use co-pilot to write go

principles.text: Use AI as a research platform to learn, not to solve your problems, or you only train yourself to prompt.
principles.quote: I should have asked it how to do those step by step and then programmed it all myself and acquired that little bit of knowledge

principles.text: Use Copilot only for code you already know how to write; if it surprises you or solves what you can't, skip it.
principles.quote: if co-pilots produce code that surprises you or if you use co-pilot to solve a problem because you don't know how you probably shouldn't use it

principles.text: Time in the saddle is the best predictor of success; build, read, and explore broadly for years.
principles.quote: time in the saddle is your like greatest indicator for you becoming successful at something

principles.text: There is no six-month path to a six-figure programming job; treat it as a marathon of about ten years.
principles.quote: I don't believe there is a six-month path to becoming some six-figure job

principles.text: Programming demands precision, so English prompts can't replace code; mostly right is wrong in code.
principles.quote: there's no mostly right in programming this is not horseshoes this is not hand grenades
